panels.visual: Greek ships sailing away over the horizon in the morning light and a gigantic wooden horse standing alone on the beach
panels.caption: After ten years the Greeks pretended to give up and left a giant wooden horse on the beach.

panels.visual: Trojan crowds coming out of the gates to look at the horse, children pointing, a celebration atmosphere
panels.caption: It was a gift, they said.

panels.visual: Cassandra (wild dark hair, wide eyes) in front of the horse warning the crowd, nobody listening, a priest Laocoön next to her
panels.caption: Cassandra warned them it would destroy the city. Nobody ever believed Cassandra.

panels.visual: Two huge sea serpents rising from the sea towards the priest Laocoön and his sons on the shore, dramatic waves, no gore shown
panels.caption: A priest called Laocoön warned them too. Sea serpents rose out of the water.

panels.visual: Trojans pulling the horse on ropes and rollers through the gates of Troy, wheels creaking, cheering
panels.caption: The Trojans dragged the horse inside the walls.

panels.visual: A hatch opening in the belly of the horse at night, Greek soldiers' helmets peeping out, moonlight
panels.caption: That night Greek soldiers climbed out of its belly.

panels.visual: The Greek soldiers opening the city gates to let the army in, torches, a sleeping town, a burning tower beginning
panels.caption: They opened the gates and burnt Troy. Odysseus had thought of the trick.

panels.visual: A modern computer screen with a picture of a horse on it and a little hand of a soldier peeking out, Glauka tapping the screen
panels.caption: A Trojan horse is also what we call a computer virus.
